title: lore check counts over-long summaries as warnings; retrieval commands stop emitting bundle-wide lint
description:
Outcome: over-long `summary` findings are reported where they belong. The ~200-character soft limit on `summary` is a lint finding, so `lore check` counts it as a warning in its summary line, and retrieval commands stop emitting bundle-wide lint.

Design (ruling by opum-doc, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-08; recorded as given -- do not redesign):
1. Summary length is a lint finding. It belongs in `lore check` as a warning, counted in its summary line.
2. `lore query` and the other retrieval commands do not emit bundle-wide lint. At most, query may note a finding on a document it actually RETURNS, never on one it did not return.
3. The ~200 threshold is unchanged. This is about where the finding is reported, not the limit.

Why: the operator reported that almost every doc gives warnings that the summary exceeds 200 characters (relayed by opum-doc ~20:35Z 2026-10-08). opum-doc measured all 13 repositories on lore 0.13.0 -- opum-doc 14 warnings, opum-agent 1, the rest 0 -- while `lore check` reports 0 warnings everywhere. So the finding is emitted by retrieval, not by the lint surface.

Reproduction (opum-agent, 2026-10-08T20:3xZ):
- `lore query "quest handoff session" --limit 1` returned stories/greenfield-claude-code-cutover, yet printed: warning: `summary` in reference/fleet-claude-code-implementation-audit.md is 208 chars; keep it under ~200 (one sentence) -- a document it did not return.
- `lore check` in the same tree printed: 23 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Related: LCLI-248 (Done) fixed the char-counting predicate in warnSummary (src/core/schema.ts), so the warning wording is stable. This task is about where that finding is reported, not how it counts.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `lore check` counts one fixture finding of EACH (a) kind -- unknown type, extra key, missing `summary`, over-long `summary` -- as a warning in its summary line (errorCount 0, warningCount reflects all four, exit 0 without --strict).
A retrieval command (`lore query`) against that fixture emits NONE of those (a) findings on stderr, for any document, returned or not.
A writer (`lore link`) emits the (a) finding for the document it WRITES and none for a document it does not (DEC-171).

plan: Reproduce on a fixture bundle: query emits the over-long-summary warning for a document it did not return; check reports 0 warnings.
lore check: add the over-long-summary finding as a warning, counted once in the summary line.
Retrieval commands (query, read, and the other bundle-loading readers): stop emitting bundle-wide frontmatter lint on stderr.
Tests: one fixture, both directions - check counts the over-long summary; query emits no summary warning for a document it did not return.
Docs: record the reporting surface (ADR-0006 sec 5 and the lint surface); run bun run lore check and bun test.
Land: PR into dev, then promote dev to main.
implementationNotes: Mechanism mapped (by reading, not assumed): retrieval commands load the WHOLE bundle via loadBundle(..., { warnings }) and flush every bundle-load warning to stderr. Those are the Tier-3 per-document frontmatter findings (unknown type, extra key, missing/over-long summary) plus structural skip advisories; `lore check` drops all warning-tier frontmatter findings (commands/check.ts:729), which is why check reported 0 while retrieval spewed them. Check-side (design point 1) DONE: extracted `overLongSummaryWarning` in core/schema.ts as the single message source; `check` now emits a warn-tier `summary-length` finding from its per-file peek; `CheckRule` extended. Tests added (positive control: one over-long summary -> warningCount 1 + summary-length finding; negative control: within-limit -> none). Verified: typecheck clean; 315 check tests + 219 schema/validate/profile tests pass. Retrieval-side (design point 2) HELD pending team-lead confirmation of the "bundle-wide lint" boundary (A: all Tier-3 per-document findings; B: summary only) -- it changes public stderr behavior across many commands, so not settled locally.
finalSummary: `lore check` now reports every per-document Tier-3 frontmatter finding -- unknown type, extra/unknown key, legacy timestamp, missing or over-long summary -- counted per file in its summary line as a warning (exit 0 unchanged; only --strict promotes it), by removing the check.ts:729 drop for warning-tier frontmatter findings rather than special-casing summaries. Nothing else emits them bundle-wide: the retrieval commands (query, read, graph, context, orphans, path, impact, tasks, export, agent) print none of them about any document; and the writers (link, sync, rename, supersede) print them ONLY for the documents they write, via a new per-path capture (frontmatterLintByPath) the bundle load fills and the writer filters by path -- not by message-text matching. Reader suppression is at the source (frontmatterLint:false threaded to the parse), not a collector filter, because several retrieval paths flatten warnings to plain strings and re-add them; the ladybug projection source is kept lint-free so a reused cached generation cannot re-emit it. Verified both directions on one fixture: check -> errorCount 0, warningCount 4, exit 0, one finding of each (a) kind; query -> returns the clean doc, stderr empty; link -> prints the warning for the doc it writes and not for another (test/link.test.ts). Full suite 4971 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; typecheck clean; biome 0 errors; bun run lore check exit 0. Ruling recorded as DEC-171 in opum-doc; cited in docs/adr/0007-validation-and-coherence.md. Landed via opum-ai/lore-cli#525.
